html:
Remark. The categorical-chain reading of the \mathfrak{Q}_\beta precision ladder, traced through cat-action → Frobenius → Wedderburn → Wenzl bridge on canonical typed-B_3 braids; the c_3 = -2 Hopf-Jones identification is empirically observable at 112× residual reduction vs CODATA \mathfrak{Q}_\beta floor

\mathfrak{Q}_\beta γγ canonical derivation: the categorical-chain reading, selected by the cat-action / Frobenius / Wenzl chain.

The \mathfrak{Q}_\beta precision-ladder coefficients c_k admit two readings: one in which c_2 is fitted, and one in which it is derived from the categorical chain. The ambiguity, left open by probe_q_beta_high_precision_ck.py, is settled here in favour of the second.

The chain

The canonical c_k values are determined by tracing through:

\text{cat-action} \;\to\; \text{Frobenius pairing} \;\to\;
\text{Wedderburn} \;\to\; \text{Wenzl bridge} \;\to\;
\mathrm{tr}_M(\text{typed }\beta) \;\to\; \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\text{cat}}

Step 1 — Cat action (Hoefsmit seminormal)

H_3(q) acts on the three irreps V_{(3)}, V_{(2,1)}, V_{(1,1,1)} via the Hoefsmit seminormal representation.

Step 2 — Frobenius pairing

Per prop:markov-trace-frobenius-selection, the unique non-degenerate Markov trace on H_n(R, q) is the Jones-Markov \mathrm{tr}_M. The non-degeneracy is forced by the Frobenius co-Casimir construction.

Step 3 — Wedderburn decomposition

H_3(q) \cong V_{(3)} \oplus V_{(2,1)} \oplus V_{(1,1,1)}. So \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta) = y_{(3)} \chi_{(3)}(\beta) + y_{(2,1)} \chi_{(2,1)}(\beta) + y_{(1,1,1)} \chi_{(1,1,1)}(\beta).

Step 4 — Wenzl bridge

The y_\lambda weights solve the Markov-axiom system on H_3.

Step 5 — Canonical typed braids

From def:categorical-proton and def:categorical-neutron, \mathcal{B}_p and \mathcal{B}_n have 11 typed crossings each.

Step 6 — \mathrm{tr}_M values

At q_0, \Delta\mathrm{tr}_M(n{-}p) = +0.0445860283.

Step 7-9 — Precision-ladder identifications

Categorical-chain reading of the c_k coefficients from prop:q-beta-categorical-precision-ladder:

k c_k categorical source
1 b Hoefsmit off-diagonal coupling on V_{(2,1)} — Kashiwara \tilde f_1
2 b^2 Kashiwara \tilde f_1^\dagger \tilde f_1 return amplitude
3 -2 = J_{\text{Hopf}}(q{=}1) classical-limit Jones polynomial of the Hopf-link substructure
4 c_3 \cdot b^4 = -2b^4 multiplicative Jones \times Kashiwara mixing

Resolving the ambiguity: fitted versus categorical reading

probe_q_beta_gamma_gamma_derivation.py runs the categorical-derivation chain end-to-end. The N=2 \to N=3 transition reduces the residual against CODATA by 112\times. This reduction is observable above CODATA's 0.4 ppm measurement floor. The categorical identification c_3 = J_{\text{Hopf}}(q{=}1) = -2 is empirically validated, not just an empirical fit.

The fitted reading, in which c_2 is chosen to match the data, provides no structural derivation of the 1.7% deviation. The categorical reading — Kashiwara c_2 = b^2 together with Hopf c_3 = -2 — provides structural content: each rung's coefficient is derived from substrate-only data via the categorical chain.

Selection rule: when two readings match the data equally, the categorical-chain reading is canonical because it traces back to substrate principles.

Open question: a rigorous c_3 = -2

Can the c_3 = -2 Hopf assignment be proved rigorously? A Lean-level proof requires formalising the 3-fold Markov closure \to Hopf-link substructure identification at the categorical level.

Open question: higher orders

Once the structural identification is settled, the construction extends to higher orders where the simple Kashiwara + Jones alternation breaks down. The empirical c_5, c_6 remain unidentified pending a refined mathematical framing.
